why:
the callback-group form of `rust:Node::create_timer_on_clock`; see that row. The group decides which `SchedContext` the callback runs under (phase 273 / RFC-0047), the clock decides what advances the timer towards its next activation, and neither implies the other. `create_timer_in_group` remains the clock-less spelling and remains WALL.

phase-427 (the `_in_group` split) -- was `rust:Node::create_timer_on_clock_in`. Rust never had the C++ ambiguity (no overloading, so no ours-only `_in` family on the node handle), but the three layers name one concept and the C ABI beneath already spelled it `_in_group` (`rclc_executor_add_timer_in_group`, `rclc_executor_add_subscription_in_group`, `nros_cpp_timer_create_in_group`). The handle's `create_timer_in_group`, `create_subscription_in_group` and `create_publisher_in_group` moved with C++ so the vocabulary is one word rather than two. RFC-0089, "The `_in` rule, amended".

KEY CORRECTED 2026-09-12 (issue 1351). This row was `rust:Node::create_timer_on_clock_in_group` and was written before the extractor could reach `NodeCtx` at all, so its key was GUESSED against the schema's own instruction -- "run the report to get the spelling; do not guess it". The guess was wrong in a way nothing could report: the correlator folds `NodeCtx` onto `Node` (`TYPE_SYNONYMS` in `scripts/api_parity/correlate.py`), so the tool emits `Node::create_timer_on_clock_in_group` and would never have met the old key. A row recorded ahead of its tool and a row for a name that does not exist are the same object, which is what 1351 was filed about.

On `nros::Node`, the executor-borrowing node handle (`exec.node_mut(id)`); it was `NodeCtx` until phase-483 W2, which the correlator folded onto `Node` (`TYPE_SYNONYMS`). MEASURABLE ONLY SINCE 2026-09-12: `nros_node::executor`'s `mod node` kept the type private while `Executor::node_mut` returned it, so every method on it was callable and none of them had ever produced a row -- issue 1351.
